subject: paper:niermann-scheres-2014
quote: It is often part of psychotherapies for adults with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, procrastination is officially not acknowledged as an ADHD-related symptom.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Captures the gap this note turns on: procrastination is clinically central to ADHD yet absent from the formal criteria.

subject: paper:niermann-scheres-2014
quote: partial correlations (corrected for the other symptom domain of ADHD) indicated that only inattention was correlated with general procrastination.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Specifies that the procrastination link is with inattention rather than impulsivity; medium confidence given the small preliminary sample (n=54).

subject: paper:rabin-2011
quote: Procrastination is increasingly viewed as involving failures in self-regulation and volition, processes commonly regarded as executive functions.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Frames procrastination as executive/self-regulatory failure; the study found EF domains predicted academic procrastination.

subject: paper:steel-2007
quote: Strong and consistent predictors of procrastination were task aversiveness, task delay, self-efficacy, and impulsiveness, as well as conscientiousness and its facets of self-control, distractibility, organization, and achievement motivation.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Meta-analytic predictors (impulsiveness, distractibility, task delay, low self-control) are precisely the ADHD cognitive profile.

subject: paper:steel-2007
quote: These effects prove consistent with temporal motivation theory, an integrative hybrid of expectancy theory and hyperbolic discounting.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Ties procrastination to hyperbolic (delay) discounting — connecting it to the reward/delay-aversion mechanism already in the graph.
